framework-expansion-card.title: A development board inside the laptop
framework-expansion-card.role: ESP32-S3 PCB, USB programming and power circuitry in the Framework expansion-card format.
framework-expansion-card.media_label: Manufactured board photography · interactive CAD assembly
framework-expansion-card.problem: Fit an ESP32 development board, its USB connection and the antenna keep-out into one Framework expansion bay.
decisions: The 0.6 mm PCB supports direct USB-C mating without a separate interposer. The module's antenna end remains unobstructed in the clear enclosure.
A CH340K provides USB serial, a BC817 pair handles automatic boot and reset, and an AMS1117-3.3 supplies the module.
framework-expansion-card.validation: The build photographs show the assembled black revision in its enclosure, close-ups of the programming and power circuit, and the earlier green PCB.
framework-expansion-card.outcome: The latest black two-layer board is assembled in the Framework shell, with the USB interface, power circuit and radio on one removable card.

framework-dual-usb.title: Two ports within one expansion bay
framework-dual-usb.role: A custom two-port USB 2.0 hub PCB packaged in the standard Framework expansion-card shell.
framework-dual-usb.media_label: Installed hardware photography · interactive CAD assembly
framework-dual-usb.problem: Fit three Type-C connectors, the hub, downstream power switching and connector protection into the outline of one laptop bay.
decisions: USB 2.0 meets the small-peripheral use case while keeping the routing and power design within the expansion-card envelope.
The CH334F implements the hub. Two TPS2065 switches limit downstream power, with USBLC6-2SC6 devices providing connector-side ESD protection.
framework-dual-usb.validation: Photographs show both sides of the assembled PCB, the two downstream ports and the card installed in a Framework laptop.
framework-dual-usb.outcome: The assembled card fits the standard clear shell and presents two Type-C ports from a single bay.

framework-raspberry-pi.title: An RP2354B within the Framework outline
framework-raspberry-pi.role: A 26 × 30 mm RP2354B microcontroller-board design for a Framework laptop expansion bay.
framework-raspberry-pi.problem: Arrange the microcontroller, USB connector, power circuit and controls around the reference enclosure's mounting points.
decisions: The 0.8 mm PCB uses a straddle-mount USB-C plug. Two tactile controls sit at the opposite edge from the connector.
The RP2354B occupies the centre of the layout, with flash, crystal and power circuitry arranged around it.
framework-raspberry-pi.outcome: The board layout and its relationship to the Framework reference enclosure are available to inspect in the CAD assembly.

framework-logic-analyser.title: Capture hardware with explicit safe states
framework-logic-analyser.role: An STM32G474 card design with board-specific capture firmware and Python host tooling.
framework-logic-analyser.media_label: CAD render · published firmware and host tests
framework-logic-analyser.problem: Bring logic and serial-bus capture into a 26 × 30 mm expansion card while keeping passive monitoring from driving the bus under observation.
decisions: Timer-triggered DMA samples the GPIO inputs. Native USB CDC carries commands and captured bytes to a Python tool that exports VCD or CSV.
The firmware boots with the muxes disconnected, CAN in standby and the multiprotocol transceiver shut down. Route changes disable the drivers before reconnecting inputs.
Raw GPIO routes are limited to 3.3 V logic. RS-232 is excluded from passive capture because that transceiver mode also enables its transmitter.
framework-logic-analyser.validation: Published host-side tests exercise binary framing, VCD/CSV export and command validation using simulated serial data. The hardware document maps firmware pins and safe states to the routed PCB.
framework-logic-analyser.outcome: The prototype firmware implements immediate capture with configured limits of 10 MS/s and 32,768 samples, plus passive Classical CAN monitoring. Hardware trigger and pre-trigger capture remain unimplemented.

tramtrace.title: From station data to the right physical LED
tramtrace.role: PCB design, embedded display logic and the vehicle-position service for the light-rail map.
tramtrace.media_label: Illuminated hardware photography · interactive CAD assembly
tramtrace.problem: Fit four light-rail lines, station labels and 116 RGB pixels onto a compact PCB, then map each live station state to its electrical position.
decisions: The hardware cross-reference links printed stations to LED chain indices. It explicitly handles the shared L2/L3 trunk and L1 Central's single route pixel.
An ESP32 and level shifter drive five LED chains. Firmware caps route brightness and the hardware-test sequence lights one route pixel at a time.
The service tracks source freshness and caches the last good data; the board clears an expired frame after 60 seconds.
tramtrace.validation: The build photographs show the assembled, illuminated map. Published mapping tests compare the 68 route/station entries with the firmware bindings, check pixel coverage and check the shared-route exceptions.
tramtrace.outcome: The physical display is accompanied by public firmware, a traced station-to-pixel map, service code and test code. The documented test-pairs sequence provides a station-by-station check of the displayed direction convention.

metroboard.title: A rail map driven by a small data contract
metroboard.role: A custom Sydney rail-map PCB and a service that converts TfNSW vehicle positions into LED states.
metroboard.media_label: Illuminated hardware photography · interactive CAD assembly
metroboard.problem: Make real-time rail activity readable on a 291-pixel PCB, with the copper, solder mask and silkscreen forming the map itself.
decisions: The service builds station-and-route keys from static GTFS data and reduces realtime vehicle positions to a compact set of LED states for the Wi-Fi-connected board.
Feed caching, per-feed retry backoff and last-good-data expiry keep the update path bounded when an upstream feed fails or rate-limits requests.
metroboard.validation: The photographs show the assembled board and illuminated routes. The public service repository includes tests for feed caching, backoff and stale-data expiry.
metroboard.outcome: A 300 × 305.7 mm physical rail display with public service and firmware source. Its PCB-as-map approach later informed the smaller TramTrace layout.

rf-test-board.title: A physical check on the RF layout
rf-test-board.maturity: Fabricated test board · 50 Ω design target
rf-test-board.role: Designed a two-layer RF comparison board and investigated its feedlines and transitions with a vector network analyser.
rf-test-board.media_label: Manufactured test-board photography · interactive CAD assembly
rf-test-board.problem: Check calculated feedline geometry against the inexpensive 1.6 mm FR-4 fabrication process used for the preceding LoRa receiver.
decisions: Place masked and unmasked coplanar traces, u.FL and SMA transitions, tuning sections and split-pi footprints on the same board.
Print the stack-up and nominal trace widths on the reverse: 1 oz copper, a 0.2 mm ground gap, and widths of 0.8877 mm with mask and 1.0244 mm without it. The design target is 50 Ω.
rf-test-board.challenges: The earlier LoRa receiver's Rev A feedline missed the intended 50 Ω impedance. Investigating it with a VNA led to this dedicated comparison board.
rf-test-board.validation: The build photographs document the test structures and their nominal geometry. The project record describes VNA investigation; quantitative traces and calibration details are not published here, so 50 Ω remains a design target.
rf-test-board.outcome: A reusable physical reference for comparing feedlines, connector transitions and filter footprints on the chosen fabrication process.

switch-mode-power-supplies.title: Power-supply testing and repair
switch-mode-power-supplies.role: Maintenance, testing and repair of low- and high-voltage power supplies and other equipment as an Electronics Engineer Trainee.
switch-mode-power-supplies.validation: My role covers power-supply maintenance, testing and repair. The photographed employer hardware is the Isolated Glitch Tester V03 and Isolated Glitch Tester Bus V02, shown from the component side, reverse and in detail.

skylabs/boards/ground-station.title: A useful flight record without depending on a laptop
skylabs/boards/ground-station.role: Ground-station PCB and receiver workflow: LoRa reception, independent storage, a field display and a phone dashboard.
skylabs/boards/ground-station.media_label: Assembled board photographs · interactive CAD assembly
skylabs/boards/ground-station.problem: Keep a second record of the aircraft telemetry and make the field controls available when a laptop is absent.
decisions: Record received packets to the ground station's own microSD card. Offer readable CSV or indexed, CRC-protected binary records alongside a rate-limited USB stream.
Put link and sensor status on the OLED, with a local Wi-Fi dashboard for pre-flight checks, log controls and event markers.
skylabs/boards/ground-station.validation: The build photographs show the assembled receiver, radio, microSD interface and reverse routing. The workflow below describes the logging and field interface; the linked aircraft diagnostic reports onboard logging results separately.

sources.label: Ground-station development, workflow and build photographs

skylabs/boards/telemetry.title: Separate the logging target from the flight result
skylabs/boards/telemetry.role: STM32 aircraft PCB, sensor acquisition, binary logging and the aircraft side of the SX1262 telemetry link.
skylabs/boards/telemetry.media_label: Assembled hardware photography · recorded flight evidence
skylabs/boards/telemetry.problem: Keep a useful onboard record while sensors update at different rates and the radio carries only a smaller live subset.
decisions: Store sensor presence and validity beside the readings, with missing measurements represented as NaN.
After the reference flight, buffer eight records per SD write and run sensor capture and logging before radio service. The logging target remains 40 Hz.
Gate EKF outputs using uncertainty and plausibility checks. The replay uses valid GNSS horizontal position and barometric height for the reference flight.
skylabs/boards/telemetry.challenges: The F110211 flight averaged 20.27 Hz against the 40 Hz target and recorded 13,402 logging overruns. Its navigation EKF diverged, so the EKF path is excluded from the flight analysis.
skylabs/boards/telemetry.validation: The published diagnostic covers 679.331 seconds and 13,772 usable aircraft records, with a 50 ms median log interval and zero SD write errors. These storage and timing results are reported separately.
skylabs/boards/telemetry.outcome: A later 150-second bench hold produced 146/146 fresh samples with continuous BNO and BME validity. The revised SD rate and EKF recovery still require confirmation in a fresh aircraft binary log.

sources.label: Flight result, changes and bench checks
